Subject: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology (post-call recap)

Hi Samir / Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful discussion. Below is a concise recap of the call, the pain we heard, the goals you stated, and suggested next steps so we can align on the technical deep dive.

Summary / pain points
- Current inference latency spikes on peak shopping hours leading to poor user experience (search/typeahead and personalization flows).
- High cost on current hosted endpoints when scale is required; need predictable unit economics for peak events.
- Concerned about privacy/compliance for PII-sensitive data in personalization models.

Goals / SLOs you described
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 200 ms for single-turn requests in the personalization flow (avg payload ~ 600 tokens including prompt).
- Sustained throughput target: ~50 req/s for production traffic, with spikes to 200 req/s during peak sale events (60-90s bursts).
- Availability SLO: 99.9% regionally; fallback plan acceptable if model variant has slightly different quality.

Model & deployment constraints
- Preference for open-weight models (cost and auditability). Mentioned interest in an 8B-15B model with quantization.
- Must support VPC/private deployment later in procurement phase; initial proof-of-concept can run in Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) in us-west.
- Need support for KV cache/prefix caching to preserve context without re-sending full prompt each time.

Initial technical approach (proposed)
- Dedicated GPU pool for primary serving (pinned model version) + Redwood-hosted small fallback (lower-cost model) for capacity overloads.
- Autoscaling/burst policy that uses a fast fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant for short bursts to keep latency within target.
- Batching windows tuned to meet p95 latency (likely sub-20ms batching windows for single-turn).

Attachments (attached to this thread)
- SLOs-draft.pdf — rough SLO matrix (p50/p95/p99 targets, tail behavior expectations).
- deployment-topology.png — suggested topology (dedicated pool with fallback).

Next steps
1) Confirm the acceptability of the p95 <= 200 ms target and peak burst assumptions (50 sustained / 200 burst).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive next week to work through model sizing, quantization tradeoffs, and exact autoscaling policy (propose Wed/Thu).
3) We (Redwood) will prepare a back-of-envelope capacity & cost estimate based on the confirmed SLOs and model choice; Marissa will include sample instance counts and rough GPU-hours.
4) Samir/Laura to share a 1-hour traffic sample (or synthetic QPS profile) and a representative prompt set (we can use it for a quick in-house baseline).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the deep dive and share an agenda. Thanks — looking forward to the next step.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Looping in a few technical notes ahead of the deep dive so we can hit the ground running:

Key assumptions I want to validate during the call:
- Median payload size: ~400-700 tokens (you mentioned ~600). If payloads trend higher, batching behavior and kernel selection will change.
- Target p95 <= 200 ms with 50 req/s sustained implies we’ll likely need 2-3 80GB A10G-equivalent instances (or their cloud-equivalents) for steady-state depending on model and quantization; burst sizing to 200 req/s will require autoscale + fast fallback.
- For prefix/KV caching: we recommend setting a 10-15 minute TTL for session caches to avoid repeated prompt resend while keeping memory bounded.

Questions for Samir/Laura to bring to the call:
- Can you share (anonymized) sample prompts for the personalization flow and the 60s QPS profile for a typical sale event?
- Do you have a hard requirement to keep model artifacts entirely on-prem / VPC (or is hybrid acceptable for POC)?

Quick note on cost estimate: I’ll run a back-of-the-envelope using 8B quantized and 13B fp16 baselines and share ranges in the pre-read.

See you on the call — I’ll bring rough instance counts and expected latency curves from our internal benchmarks.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
